title: Dizzy and Lorraine persuade him to go to Europe
summary: Dizzy wanted him for the European trip since Joe Harris was not working; Clarke refused until Lorraine Gillespie asked him in person.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: And one day -- well, they had Joe Harris was playing with the band, Diz's band, at the time. And something that Joe was doing that wasn't comfortable for Dizzy, you know, the rhythm section wasn't comfortable.
So he asked me would I make the trip to Europe with him.
And I said, 'Oh, Diz, I can't do that. I'm with Tadd, and we have our little thing going, you know.'

Which was -- we had Ernie Henry. Oh, we had a good group. We would change, you know, frequently. And I said, 'Oh, no, man, Diz, I can't make it.' So he said, 'Oh, don't be a drag, Klook, come on. Come on.' I said, 'No. I'm happy with Tadd, Diz, and you do your thing, and we're still boys. We'll always be friends, you know, as long as I live. But I don't -- I'm not in the mood to go to Europe. I just left Europe in the Army.'
Yeah. I wanted to stay home with my wife and all.

So he said, 'Okay, but you're still a drag.' So he goes and gets Lorraine and brings Lorraine down the next night. So Lorraine says, 'Kenny, I'd like to talk to you.' So in the back of my mind I was thinking -- because you know, I love Lorraine, you know. So Lorraine says, 'Now, listen Kenny, we need you to make this trip. It's very important. It's going to be a very important trip, and we would like for you to
make it." Then I began to think, you know. I said, "Now, what is this." You know. So before the night was over I told her okay, I'll go.
